claims.description: Dry-run derives the current envelope matrix demand, checked-in baseline sum, and 10% headroom without truncation.

Runner tests prove per-flow attempted, completed, budget-skipped, and required-sample accounting, including a flow that reports incomplete because a pre-call skip drops attempted below required with zero budget-skips.

Gate tests prove zero/partial exhaustion fails closed while incomplete coverage is excluded from BaselineDrift, an incomplete flow absent from baseline.json still fails the coverage gate, and --update-baseline refuses to accept (gate) or write (index.ts seed-guard) incomplete coverage.
Index summary code prints configured versus required demand and per-flow coverage.

Pure mastery budget tests cover the complete grid, changed counts, 215 rejection, 216 acceptance, and derive that 216 configured versus 192 expected leaves exactly three 8-call reproduce rounds for one offender.

Workflow comments record matrix-derived envelope provider demand including internal judge calls, sequential estimated provider demand, and gate-specific caps. Timeout re-verification: the comment projects each gate's retained-run-30721918215 wall clock (envelope 839s, teaching 271s, mastery 710s) onto CURRENT demand via ratios grounded in that run's own log (envelope 366/300, teaching 5/5, mastery 24/21) to ~35.1 min / ~5.1x headroom under the unchanged 180-minute timeout-minutes, with explicit uncertainty (single run, no P90, 2 failed envelope OUTER invocations, queue/latency variance, and a disclosure that 29 of that run's 33 skips were budget-exceeded - 10 judge-bearing cases and 19 non-judge-bearing cases, not all 29 judge-bearing). No paid live run performed; timeout-minutes itself unchanged. Review-fix round 1 (M1+S1): parsed timeout-minutes instead of hardcoding 180 (mutation-proven); labeled the 300 denominator as an outer-invocation cap, not a measured provider-call count. Review-fix round 2 (SHOULD-1/2): replaced loose ratio toContain checks with numBoundary-guarded regexes (superset-proof); added the 29-skip disclosure. Skip-split correction round (1 MUST_FIX): the round-2 disclosure's 16/13 split was itself wrong - it conflated FLOW-level judge-bearing (safety-probes/language-quality) with CASE-level (only legitimate_sensitive-category safety-probes cases are judge-bearing). Independently re-derived from the current registry: the 10 skipped safety-probes cases are the tail of the 17yo-french-advanced profile's enumeration order, of which 4 are legitimate_sensitive; all 6 skipped language-quality cases are judge-bearing (providerCallCount unconditionally 2, and 6 is the flow's entire current scenario count). Corrected split: 4+6=10 judge-bearing, 6+3+10=19 non-judge-bearing. A new test assertion derives this split from safetyProbesFlow.enumerateScenarios and the language-quality registry rather than hardcoding 10/19, proven by a 16-mutation RED then byte-identical revert GREEN.
Deterministic workflow-contract tests pin derived provider-demand relationships, omitted-cap preflight ordering, runtime order, and changed counts without a fixed envelope-only assertion.
